market_holds: Spot about $84.1 (Yahoo bars, 2026-11-18 intraday), -14.2% over 5 sessions, -19.9% over 20, at a 52-week low and 55% below the high (sealed baseline). The fall tracks the whole retail-broker and crypto complex rather than anything specific to Futu: HOOD fell from 81.35 to 68.89 over the same five sessions and from 104 to 69 since 10-15, BTC from about 80k to 62.7k, NVDA from 186.6 to 152.8 (Yahoo daily closes I pulled). The Nov-20 options price about a 7% move including two ordinary days, so roughly 6% for the event. I took that from the 82.45-strike straddle at mid, about $5.95 on $84.09; the ATM 85 call has no market. Skew is near flat (+1.3 vol points at the seal) and put/call OI 0.9. Consensus is thin and inconsistent. FXEmpire/Chartmill have 4 analysts at HK$6.89B revenue (about -4% QoQ) and HK$23.09 EPS per ADS (about -13% QoQ); Earnings Whispers (2026-11-11) has $814.8M, which is -11% QoQ. Management's August guide was that Q3-to-date volume was 'down modestly' sequentially, net adds were moderating and CAC was rising, with the target of 800k net adds for the year kept. The CSRC penalty of about RMB1.85B was already accrued in Q1 (2026-05-28 release), so it is not a Q3 P&L risk. History in the full close-to-close window: Aug-2026 +3.0% (opened +7.5%, then +9.7% the next day), Mar-2026 -6.3%, Nov-2025 -1.1% (opened +2.3%), Aug-2025 +6.0%.
view: The quarter itself (July to September) is probably near consensus or slightly ahead of it. US retail activity held up: Robinhood had record Q3 equity notional of $992B against $956B in Q2 (+4%) and record options at 905M against 774M (+17%). Hong Kong was weaker, with HKEX headline ADT -12% QoQ. Futu's US volume is about 78% of its total, so the 'down modestly' guide fits roughly -5 to -10% total volume. Client assets should rise QoQ: the HSI was +7.6% and the Nasdaq +2.5% over Q3, and management said the mainland outflow was mostly taken in June and July. Interest income should also rise, because one-month HIBOR rose to about 2.95% by mid-September and the HKMA base rate was raised. That makes the HK$6.89B consensus beatable. It is not a stale bar, though: management set it with its own soft guide. The stock will trade on the Q4-to-date commentary, net adds and client assets, not on Q3. Here the evidence points both ways. October activity was firm: IBKR October DARTs were +5% m/m and Robinhood said October ADVs were within 5% of Q3 records. Hong Kong October ADT was HK$180.7B against HK$201.9B in September. November has been a risk-off rout, so client assets and margin balances are lower (the Nasdaq is about -9% and the HSI about -4.5% since Sep 30), while volatility tends to lift trading volume. The 20% fall into the print has already priced a lot of sector-wide softness. A firm Q3 with a buyback at about 6-7x run-rate earnings could bring a relief bounce, but whatever the sector and crypto do between the close and 13:00 ET dominates the window. I see no dated datapoint the price clearly lacks.

recommendation.reason: The Q3 numbers probably land near or a little above a consensus the company's own August guide set. The Q4-to-date line is mixed: firm October activity against falling November asset values. The stock's recent fall is sector and crypto beta, not a Futu-specific datapoint the market has missed. No mechanism clears the 65% bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q4-to-date commentary that quantifies trading volume up QoQ with net adds on pace for 800k would make a relief rally likely (long). A disclosed new mainland restriction, client-asset outflow or net-add miss would make it short.

self_critique: I may be underweighting the oversold setup. A stock at 6-7x earnings, down 20% in a month on sector beta, can rip on any reassuring KPI (assets up QoQ, a buyback), as it did in August when it opened +7.5%. The other side is that the November rout makes the Q4-to-date client-asset figure look bad, and with risk-off momentum this strong the tape into 13:00 ET could swamp any print. I don't think either reading clearly beats the other, so I stay near 50.
approach_notes: P4 (show it is priced) helped: the consensus was set off management's own soft guide, so a beat is not unpriced. Pulling peer tapes and peer operating data (P3 stakeholders) was the fastest way to separate beta from information. The playbook gives no guidance for a name whose recent move is mostly sector beta and whose window is short.
